title: Implement reusable catalog JSON codec
description: Implement the standalone version-1 reusable catalog codec used by flat-file storage. Read and write {version:1,definitions:[...]} deterministically with ordered definitions, strict supported-version checking, unknown and duplicate property rejection, canonical UTC RFC3339Nano timestamps, UTF-8 preservation, and validation through the core catalog contract. Treat a missing file as an empty catalog without creating it during reads; reject empty, malformed, or semantically invalid definitions when a file exists. Add table-driven codec tests for round trips, deterministic bytes, Unicode instructions, unsupported versions, duplicate names with mixed case, malformed IDs/timestamps, and unknown fields. Do not connect the codec to provider methods yet.

comments.author: codex-wtp-loop
comments.message: Scope confirmed: add a standalone internal/reusablejson codec plus focused table-driven tests only. It will validate core.ReusableTaskCatalog, preserve definition order and Unicode, emit compact deterministic JSON with canonical UTC timestamps, reject unknown/duplicate properties and invalid existing files, and expose missing-file-as-empty reads without wiring provider methods.

comments.author: codex-wtp-loop
comments.message: Implemented internal/reusablejson/json.go and table-driven json_test.go. Encode validates the core catalog, preserves definition order and UTF-8 text, and emits compact deterministic {version,definitions} JSON with canonical UTC RFC3339Nano timestamps. Decode strictly rejects unknown/duplicate properties, unsupported versions, malformed values, non-UTC timestamps, and semantic catalog violations. ReadFile maps only a missing path to EmptyReusableTaskCatalog without creating storage; existing empty/malformed files fail. WriteFile uses codec bytes and creates parents only on writes. Provider methods and integration remain untouched. Verification passed: gofmt, go test -count=1 ./..., go test -race ./internal/reusablejson ./internal/core, go vet ./..., and git diff --check.
